summary: Vladimir Ivanov Georgiev was a linguist who studied at Sofia University under Stefan Mladenov, the University of Vienna, Humboldt University of Berlin, Florence, and Paris. He served at Sofia University as Assistant (1931), Docent (1936), and Head of Linguistics (1945–1974).

Vladimir Ivanovich Kalyanov was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Leningrad Institute of History, Philosophy and Linguistics under Aleksej Petrovič Barannikov and Theodore Stcherbatsky. He worked at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts (1937–1985) and Saint Petersburg State University (1938–1941).

Vladimir Minorsky worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and history. He studied law at Moscow Imperial University and at the Lazarev Institute of Oriental Languages. He taught at INALCO, SOAS University of London (Lecturer 1932, Professor 1937–1944), and Cairo University (1948–1949).

Vladimir Nikolaevich Toporov was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Moscow State University under Mikhail Nikolayevich Peterson. Beginning in 1954, he worked as a naučnyj sotrudnik and from 1960 as a staršij naučnyj sotrudnik at the Institute of Slavic Studies.

Vladimir P. Ivanov is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He was a senior researcher at the St. Petersburg Institute for Informatics and Automation in 1989 and is attested in 2009 as a Research Fellow at the Institute of Oriental Studies.

Vladimir Svjatoslavovič Vorob’ëv-Desjatovskij was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Aleksej Petrovič Barannikov. He served as a naučnyj sotrudnik at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts (1951–1956) and taught Sanskrit at Saint Petersburg State University.

Vladimir Tikhonov works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Educated at Saint Petersburg State University, Moscow State University, and Korea University, he taught at Kyung Hee University before becoming Associate Professor (2000) and Professor (2006) at the University of Oslo.

Vladimír Miltner was an Indologist and linguist who completed his Ph.D. studies at Charles University between 1952 and 1967. In 1967, he held a post as a research scholar at the Czech Academy of Sciences.

Volker Caumanns is a Tibetologist who earned his MA at Hamburg under David P. Jackson and his PhD at Munich under Franz-Karl Ehrhard. He held posts at Munich (2006–2012), LIRI (2012–2015), and is attested at Bern, Hamburg, and Leipzig.

Volker Grabowsky is a historian who studied at Kiel University and Chiang Mai University. He held positions at the University of Passau, National University of Laos, and University of Münster, before becoming chair holder in Thai studies at the University of Hamburg in 2009.

Volker Zotz works in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Vienna and under Anagarika Govinda, later holding academic posts at Vienna, Otani, Ryukoku, Saarland, and Luxembourg universities.

Vrajavallabha Dvivedi worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He headed the Yogatantra Department at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and served as Deputy Director at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 1990–1992).
Vriti Sharma works in computational fields and Indology. She has held posts at the Indian Institute of Technology Mandi and BharatGen.

Vsevolod Bronislavovich Tomashevsky was a linguist who studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Jan Niecisław Baudouin de Courtenay and Vincenz Scherzl. He taught at Baku State University before serving as Professor of Comparative Linguistics and Rector at Saint Petersburg State University.

Vsevolod Miller was a scholar of Iranian, Indological, and linguistic studies. He studied at Moscow State University under Pavel Jakovlevič Petrov and Fyodor Buslaev, later becoming Docent there, Director of the Lazarev Institute of Oriental Languages, and Russian Academy of Sciences member.

Vsevolod Sergeevič Semencov worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Moscow State University's Institute of Asian and African Studies and Banaras Hindu University, then served as naučnyj sotrudnik at the Moscow Institute of Oriental Studies and the Institute of Philosophy.

Vyacheslav Ivanov was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Moscow State University under Mikhail Nikolayevich Peterson and Pyotr Kuznetsov. He held positions at Moscow State University, the Institute of Slavic Studies, UCLA, Stanford, Yale, and Russian State University for the Humanities.

Vydūnas worked in philosophy and Indology, studying at Königsberg, Greifswald, Halle-Wittenberg, Leipzig, and Humboldt University of Berlin. He taught Lithuanian at Humboldt University of Berlin (1917–1919) and held a post at the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen (~1917–1940).

Václav Machek was a linguist and Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at Charles University under Josef Zubatý, later studying under Meillet, Bloch, and Lévi. He was a librarian at the Slovakian Library in Paris and became Docent at Masaryk University in 1931.
W. F. Jayasuriya is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Rerukane Ariyaratne, H. D. Dharmasiriwardhana, and M. U. Sri Kaveeswara.
